+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Check that the phone number, email, and profile link are live and professional.
items.because: A recruiter needs to be able to reach you.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality for US applications unless specifically requested.
items.because: They generally do not help assess your qualifications.

items.says: Put Brightcart before Pinecrest.
items.because: Reverse chronological order makes your most recent work easiest to find.

items.says: Checking the p-value daily and stopping at the first result below 0.05 does not support an ordinary 5% significance claim.
items.because: That stopping rule is optional stopping.

items.says: If retaining the A/B test, explain what decision it informed.
Clarify your contribution to the staffing decision if others implemented it.
items.because: The impact should be credible without overstating ownership.

items.says: Change the present-tense verb to past tense.
Substantiate how the reduction in query errors was measured.
Focus the bullet on the fraud-extract automation and its monthly saving.
items.because: The other duties obscure that achievement.

items.says: Clarify what drove the increase in repeat purchases.
items.because: The current causal claim is stronger than the bullet establishes.

items.says: Specify whether “3 days” was elapsed time rather than three full days of work.
items.because: That makes the comparison with two hours fair.

items.says: A null customer name does not establish that a customer has no orders.
items.because: The method requires checking for a missing order after joining from customers.

items.says: Make your action the subject of the bullet.
Shorten the opening.
Clarify whether you used dbt or SQL models with a similar structure.
Define what “orders tied to a campaign” means if the metric is important to the role.
Add what the funded recommendations achieved if you know it.
items.because: That outcome would be stronger than funding alone.

items.says: Clarify the comparison period or measurement behind “halving.”
Mean absolute error is presented as a percentage rather than in the forecast quantity’s units.
items.because: Mean absolute error normally has the same units as the quantity forecast.

items.says: Identify the metric actually used and, if applicable, how forecasts were tested on unseen dates.
The reduction from 300 to 200 is 33%, not 50%.
Make clear that the reduction was in a historical replay, not live operations.
Define what counts as a forecast “hit.”
The change from 60% to 75% is 15 percentage points, not a 15% relative increase.
Clarify whether the line fell after the shift change.
Explain how the reduction in line time was measured.
Check whether “9,000” refers to individual logs or visit records and use the accurate term.
Add tools you actually used and can discuss, particularly a dashboard platform or dbt if applicable.
Make sure the methods list reflects work you can confidently explain after correcting the forecasting metrics and A/B-test bullet.
